title: Join two lists side by side
description: names.txt holds one user name per line and roles.txt holds the matching role on the same line number. Print them side by side: line 1 of names.txt with line 1 of roles.txt, then line 2 with line 2, and so on, joining each pair with a single colon. Example: alice and admin -> alice:admin. Print one pair per line, in file order, and nothing else. The default separator is not a colon, so the colon has to be asked for explicitly.
objective: Practise merging files line by line as columns with a custom delimiter.
check:
expected='alice:admin
bob:viewer
carol:editor'
if [ "$(cat "$CMM_STDOUT")" != "$expected" ]; then
  echo "Expected each name joined to its role by a colon, in file order:"
  echo "$expected"
  echo "Got:"
  cat "$CMM_STDOUT"
  exit 1
fi

title: Fold a word list into one line
description: words.txt holds one word per line. Print all of its words on a single line, in file order, separated by exactly one space: no tab between words, no space before the first word or after the last. Example: the lines The, quick, brown, fox -> The quick brown fox. By default the words would be joined with tabs, so the space separator has to be asked for explicitly.
objective: Practise turning the lines of one file into a single delimited line.
check:
expected='The quick brown fox jumps'
if [ "$(cat "$CMM_STDOUT")" != "$expected" ]; then
  echo "Expected every word on one line, separated by single spaces:"
  echo "$expected"
  echo "Got:"
  cat -et "$CMM_STDOUT"
  echo "(Tabs show as ^I and line ends as \$ above.)"
  exit 1
fi
